mainTopic: The end of רציעה for an עבד עברי, and the ways a עבד כנעני is acquired and freed: money, document, חזקה, חליפין, משיכה and service acts.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the ברייתא on רציעה of an עבד עברי. The awl goes through the ear and straight into the door in one boring, and the door must be standing and attached like a מזוזה. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי explains why the ear is pierced: it heard at הר סיני that Jews are servants of ה׳ alone. רבי שמעון בר רבי explains why the door and doorpost are used: they witnessed the Jews going free in מצרים. A new משנה then teaches that a עבד כנעני is acquired with money, a document, or חזקה. רבי מאיר and חכמים disagree about how he goes free. The גמרא learns these methods from a היקש to an inherited field, adds חליפין and שמואל's משיכה, and explains why calling works for an animal or a minor slave but not an adult slave. It then defines חזקה as the slave serving the master, and רב אשי explains the disagreement about lifting. The amud ends with מר זוטרא using a service act to acquire the slave of a dying גר, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What we might have thought if the verse said 'his ear to the door'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says that if the פסוק had only said "אזנו בדלת," we might think only the door is pierced, opposite the ear, and not the ear itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the verse had said "his ear in the door," I would have said: he pierces the door at the spot opposite his ear. The door, yes; his ear, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is explaining why the פסוק uses the exact words "באזנו ובדלת." It first shows a mistaken reading we might have had with different wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the wording "his ear to the door," one could read it as marking a spot on the door next to the ear. Under that reading, only the door gets pierced. This sets up the reason the real wording was needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Had it been said; if the verse had worded it this way
I would have said (a mistaken first thought)

phrases.english: Had it said "his ear in the door,"
I would have said:
he should pierce into the door, opposite his ear.
The door, yes; his ear, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's explanation of "ונתתה באזנו ובדלת" from before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hypothetical reading: with the wording "אזנו בדלת," only the door would be pierced.

steps.title: But another verse says the ear is pierced
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the mistaken idea. How could we think the ear is not pierced, when a different פסוק clearly says "ורצע אדניו את אזנו"?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the ear is not pierced? But it is written: "And his master shall pierce his ear with an awl"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the 'mistaken thought' from step 1. Nobody could ever have thought the ear is left alone, because a פסוק says the ear is pierced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'what I would have thought' must still make sense. Since שמות 21:6 says the ear is pierced, the idea that only the door is pierced could never have come up. So the ברייתא's first idea needs to be explained differently.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? (brings a verse as a challenge)
An awl, a sharp boring tool

phrases.english: And the ear, not?
But isn't it written:
"And his master shall pierce his ear with an awl"!
phrases.notes: שמות 21:6

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the mistaken reading in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that only the door is pierced and not the ear.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An explicit פסוק says the ear is pierced, so that first idea is impossible.

steps.title: The real mistaken thought: pierce the ear first, then the door separately
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes what the mistaken thought was. We might have thought the ear is pierced away from the door, and afterward the ear is placed on the door and the door is pierced at that spot.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, I would have said: he pierces the ear outside, then places it on the door, and pierces the door opposite his ear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by restating the mistaken idea. Both ear and door are pierced, but in two separate steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the first idea fits with שמות 21:6, because the ear is pierced. The mistake is only about how it is done: two separate piercings instead of one continuous one.

phrases.english: Rather: I would have said
he pierces the ear outside
phrases.notes: "Outside" means not at the door; he pierces the ear on its own first.

phrases.english: and places it on the door,
and pierces into the door, opposite his ear,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2 by redefining the mistaken thought of step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the door is pierced, not the ear.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are pierced, but in the mistaken view they could be pierced separately.

steps.title: The verse teaches: one continuous piercing through the ear into the door
steps.stepSummary: The words "באזנו ובדלת" teach that the awl goes through the ear and keeps going until it reaches the door.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore the verse says: "through his ear and into the door." How so? He keeps boring until he reaches the door.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the real rule that the wording "באזנו ובדלת" teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two separate steps are ruled out. The ear must be on the door while it is pierced, and one push of the awl goes through the ear and into the door.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches; therefore the verse says
How so? How does this work?

steps.whatToRemember: רציעה is one continuous piercing: the awl goes through the ear while it rests on the door, and it keeps going into the door.

phrases.english: therefore the verse says: "through his ear and into the door" —
phrases.notes: דברים 15:17

phrases.english: How so?

phrases.aramaic: דּוֹקֵר וְהוֹלֵךְ עַד שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ אֵצֶל דֶּלֶת.
phrases.english: He keeps boring until he reaches the door.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the mistaken idea of step 3 with the פסוק's wording.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ear is pierced while on the door, in one continuous boring into the door.

steps.title: The door must be attached and upright, like a doorpost
steps.stepSummary: Any door might seem good enough, even one taken off its hinges. The word "מזוזה" teaches that the door must be upright and attached, like a doorpost.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Door": I might think it means either a detached door or one that is not detached. Therefore the verse says "doorpost": just as a doorpost stands upright, so too the door must stand upright.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a new detail. It explains what kind of door counts for רציעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "דלת" alone could include a loose door lying on the ground. Because the פסוק puts "מזוזה" next to the door, the two are compared. A doorpost is always fixed in place, so the door must be standing and attached too.

phrases.english: "Door" — I might understand:
whether detached or not detached,
therefore the verse says: "doorpost" —
phrases.notes: שמות 21:6

phrases.english: just as a doorpost is upright,
so too the door must be upright.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how the piercing is done to which door qualifies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The door used for רציעה must be upright and attached, like a מזוזה.

steps.title: Why is the ear chosen over every other body part?
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי explains the פסוק as a symbolic lesson. He asks why the ear, of all body parts, is the one that gets pierced.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי would explain this verse as a kind of symbolic lesson: Why is the ear different from all the other limbs of the body?
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. It is about the meaning behind the law, not about how to do it. This step asks the question, and the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the ברייתא dealt with the details of the procedure. Now רבן יוחנן בן זכאי looks for the message of the מצוה by asking why it is specifically the ear.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a kind of ornament, meaning a symbolic or allegorical teaching
What is different? Why is this one special?

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי הָיָה דּוֹרֵשׁ
phrases.english: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai would expound
this verse as a kind of ornament:
phrases.notes: He means a symbolic lesson, a teaching that brings out the deeper message.

phrases.english: Why is the ear different
from all the limbs in the body?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי הָיָה דּוֹרֵשׁ אֶת הַמִּקְרָא הַזֶּה כְּמִין חוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the halachic details of רציעה to the meaning behind it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the ear in particular is pierced.

steps.title: The ear that heard at Sinai 'they are My servants' is pierced
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ says: this ear heard at הר סיני that Jews are servants to Me and not servants of servants. Since this man went and took a human master, let that ear be pierced.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא said: The ear that heard My voice on הר סיני when I said "For the children of Israel are servants to Me," meaning not servants to servants, and this man went and acquired a master for himself, let it be pierced.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the answer to רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's question. The ear is pierced because it heard, and ignored, the message that a Jew belongs to ה׳ alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק "כי לי בני ישראל עבדים" teaches that a Jew should serve only ה׳. The servant who chooses to stay with his master has given himself to a human master, so the ear that heard this message is marked.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He

steps.whatToRemember: The ear is pierced because it heard at הר סיני that Jews are servants of ה׳ alone, yet this man chose a human master.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that staying a servant by choice is not seen as a good thing. The רציעה is a sign of this mistake.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:

phrases.aramaic: אֹזֶן שֶׁשָּׁמְעָה קוֹלִי עַל הַר סִינַי
phrases.english: The ear that heard My voice on Mount Sinai
when I said:
"For the children of Israel are servants to Me" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:55

phrases.english: and not servants to servants,
and this one went and acquired a master for himself —
let it be pierced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ear heard at Sinai that Jews serve ה׳ alone, yet this man took a human master, so that ear is pierced.

steps.title: Why the door and doorpost?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בר רבי gives another symbolic lesson. He asks why the door and doorpost, out of everything in the house, are used for the piercing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בר רבי would explain this פסוק as a beautiful symbolic lesson: Why are the door and doorpost different from every other object in the house?
steps.whatsHappening: Right after רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's lesson about the ear, a second חכם asks a matching question about the door and doorpost. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי asked why the ear is the body part that gets pierced. Now רבי שמעון בר רבי asks why the piercing happens at the door and doorpost. The question is about the meaning behind the law, not about how the law works.

keyTerms.meaning: explains a פסוק to draw out a lesson
like a decorative wreath; a beautiful symbolic explanation

phrases.english: And רבי שמעון, the son of רבי,
would explain this verse
like a kind of decorative wreath:
phrases.notes: This is the same phrase used for רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's lesson. It means a lovely symbolic explanation, not a legal ruling.

phrases.english: Why are the door and the doorpost different
from all the other objects in the house?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה נִשְׁתַּנָּה דֶּלֶת וּמְזוּזָה מִכׇּל כֵּלִים שֶׁבַּבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's question about the ear (Step 6), now asked about the door and doorpost from Step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the symbolic reason that the piercing takes place at the door and doorpost?

steps.title: The door and doorpost were witnesses in מצרים
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ says the door and doorposts witnessed Him passing over the Jewish homes in מצרים and making the Jews His servants. This man took a human master, so he is pierced in front of those witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: ה׳ said: The door and doorpost were witnesses in מצרים when I passed over the lintel and the two doorposts. I said, 'The Jews are My servants,' and not servants of servants. I took them out from slavery to freedom. Yet this man went and got himself a master. So let him be pierced in front of them.
steps.whatsHappening: This step answers the question: the door and doorpost are the witnesses to the Jews becoming ה׳'s servants. That is why the man is pierced in front of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer matches the answer about the ear. The ear heard the message at הר סיני, and the doorposts saw it happen in מצרים. Both the ear and the door were present when the Jews were made ה׳'s servants, so both take part in marking the man who chose a human master.

keyTerms.meaning: lintel; the beam above the door

steps.whatToRemember: The ear heard the message at סיני and the door and doorposts saw it in מצרים. Both were there when the Jews became ה׳'s servants, so the man who took a human master is pierced with both.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
The door and doorpost, which were witnesses in Egypt
at the time that I passed over the lintel
and over the two doorposts,
and I said: "For the children of Israel are servants to Me" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:55

phrases.english: and not servants to servants,
and I brought them out from slavery to freedom,
and this man went and acquired a master for himself —
let him be pierced in front of them.
phrases.notes: "Them" means the door and doorpost, the witnesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: דֶּלֶת וּמְזוּזָה שֶׁהָיוּ עֵדִים בְּמִצְרַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The door and doorposts witnessed ה׳ taking the Jews as His servants in מצרים. The man who took a human master is pierced before those witnesses.

steps.title: New משנה: how a עבד כנעני is acquired and freed, according to רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that a עבד כנעני is acquired with money, a document, or taking possession. According to רבי מאיר, he goes free with money given by others or with a document he receives himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A Canaanite slave is acquired with money, a document, or taking possession. He can acquire himself, meaning his freedom, with money given through others, or with a document received by himself. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new משנה about the עבד כנעני, a non-Jewish slave. It lists the three ways to acquire him and gives רבי מאיר's view on how he goes free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two parts here. The first part, how he is acquired, has no argument. The second part is רבי מאיר's view on freeing him: money works only when others give it, but a document works when the slave receives it himself.

keyTerms.meaning: a non-Jewish slave owned by a Jew
money, document, taking possession: the three ways of acquiring
acquires himself, meaning he gains his freedom

steps.confusionAlert: "קונה את עצמו" does not mean the slave buys himself as property. It means he becomes free.

phrases.english: משנה: A Canaanite slave is acquired
with money, with a document, and with taking possession,
and he acquires himself
phrases.notes: He means the slave gains his freedom.

phrases.english: with money through others,
and with a document by himself,
these are the words of רבי מאיר.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ עֶבֶד כְּנַעֲנִי נִקְנֶה בְּכֶסֶף וּבִשְׁטָר וּבַחֲזָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה; a new topic after the end of the עבד עברי discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A עבד כנעני is acquired with money, a document, or taking possession. According to רבי מאיר, he goes free with money given by others or with a document he receives himself.

steps.title: חכמים: how the slave goes free
steps.stepSummary: חכמים reverse רבי מאיר: money works when the slave gives it himself, and a document works through others. The money must belong to others, though.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: With money given by himself, and with a document received through others, as long as the money belongs to others.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the other side of the מחלוקת in the משנה. חכמים give their own view of how a עבד כנעני goes free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים say the slave himself can hand over the money, and a document works when others receive it. They add one condition: the money must come from other people, not from the slave.

keyTerms.meaning: as long as; on condition that

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
with money by himself
and with a document through others,
as long as the money belongs to others.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: בְּכֶסֶף עַל יְדֵי עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing opinion to רבי מאיר in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to חכמים, the slave goes free with money he gives himself (if the money belongs to others) or with a document received through others.

steps.title: What is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn the three ways of acquiring a עבד כנעני.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the source in the תורה for the first line of the משנה. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about the first line, that a עבד כנעני is acquired with money, a document, or taking possession. The משנה stated the rule without a source, so the גמרא wants to find one in a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do we know it?

phrases.english: גמרא: From where do we know this?
phrases.notes: He is asking about the first line of the משנה: the three ways of acquiring the slave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה in Step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches that a עבד כנעני is acquired with money, a document, or taking possession.

steps.title: The slave is compared to an inherited field
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק compares a עבד כנעני to a שדה אחוזה. Just as a field is acquired with money, a document, or taking possession, so is the slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "And you shall bequeath them to your children after you, to inherit as a possession." The פסוק compares the slaves to an inherited field. Just as an inherited field is acquired with money, a document, or taking possession, so too a Canaanite slave is acquired with money, a document, or taking possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a היקש, a comparison made by the פסוק itself. The slave is compared to an inherited field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the word אחוזה, the same word used for land, when it talks about slaves. Because of that link, the three ways of acquiring land are applied to a עבד כנעני.

keyTerms.meaning: He compared them; from הֶקֵּשׁ, a comparison made by the פסוק
and you shall pass them down as an inheritance

phrases.english: As it is written: "And you shall bequeath them to your children
after you, to inherit as a possession" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:46

phrases.english: The verse compared them to an inherited field.
Just as an inherited field is acquired
with money, with a document, and with taking possession —
so too a Canaanite slave is acquired
with money, with a document, and with taking possession.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: וְהִתְנַחַלְתֶּם אֹתָם לִבְנֵיכֶם אַחֲרֵיכֶם לָרֶשֶׁת אֲחֻזָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מנלן of Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A היקש from ויקרא 25:46 compares the slave to a שדה אחוזה, which is acquired with money, a document, or taking possession.

steps.title: Should the slave also return in יובל?
steps.stepSummary: If the slave is compared to a field, then maybe he should also go back to his original owner in יובל, the way a field does.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as an inherited field returns to its owners in יובל, should a Canaanite slave also return to his owners in יובל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the comparison it just made by pushing it too far. If the slave is like a field in every way, he should also go back in יובל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An inherited field that was sold goes back to its original family in יובל. If the היקש is complete, the same should be true of the slave. That would mean the sale of a slave is never permanent.

phrases.english: If so, just as an inherited field
returns to its owners in the יובל year —
so too a Canaanite slave
should return to his owners in the יובל year?
phrases.notes: "His owners" means the person who sold him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה חוֹזֶרֶת לַבְּעָלִים בַּיּוֹבֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the היקש of Step 13 goes.
steps.kashyaTarget: The היקש between a עבד כנעני and a שדה אחוזה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison is complete, the field's rule of returning in יובל should apply to the slave too.

steps.title: The slave is owned forever
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the slaves serve forever. So the comparison to a field does not include returning in יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק teaches: "Forever you shall make them serve."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with another phrase from the same פסוק. It shows that the slave does not go back in יובל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לעולם, forever, shows that the sale of a עבד כנעני is permanent. The היקש still teaches how he is acquired, but it does not bring along the יובל rule.
steps.whatToRemember: A עבד כנעני is acquired the same ways as a field: money, a document, or taking possession. But unlike a field, he stays with his owner forever and does not return in יובל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a היקש can carry over some rules but not others, when another phrase in the פסוק limits it.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"Forever you shall make them serve."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:46, the same פסוק as before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A separate phrase in the פסוק limits the היקש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The היקש might make the slave return to his owner in יובל, like a field.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word לעולם shows the slave is owned permanently. The היקש only teaches the ways of acquiring him.

steps.title: A ברייתא adds a fourth method: חליפין
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a עבד כנעני can also be acquired through חליפין.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: a slave can also be acquired through חליפין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that adds another way to acquire a עבד כנעני, beyond the three ways listed in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה listed money, a document, and taking possession. This ברייתא says חליפין, a symbolic exchange where an object such as a cloth is handed over, also works. This sets up the question of why our משנה left it out.

keyTerms.meaning: Symbolic exchange, usually done by handing over a cloth

phrases.english: It was taught: also through symbolic exchange.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a method of acquisition that our משנה did not list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A עבד כנעני can also be acquired through חליפין.

steps.title: Why does our משנה leave out חליפין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why our תנא did not mention חליפין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our תנא, why doesn't he list it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why our משנה's author did not include חליפין, if it really works for a slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If חליפין works, the list in the משנה looks incomplete. The גמרא wants to know why the omission makes sense.

phrases.english: And our tanna?
phrases.notes: He means: why didn't the author of our משנה list חליפין too?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges our משנה based on the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The list of three methods in our משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If חליפין works for a slave, the משנה's list looks incomplete.

steps.title: Our משנה only lists methods that are new for a slave
steps.stepSummary: Our תנא only lists methods that do not work for movable objects, since those are the surprising ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: He teaches only methods that do not work for movable property; methods that do work for movable property he does not teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that our משנה only bothers to list methods that are surprising for a slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might assume a slave is acquired the way movable objects are. So methods that do not work for movables, like money and a document, are worth teaching. חליפין already works for movables, so it is obvious and the משנה skips it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not / it is (it applies or doesn't apply)

phrases.english: A matter that does not apply to movable property, he teaches;
a matter that does apply to movable property, he does not teach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why our משנה left out חליפין.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines what the משנה chose to include
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה lists only methods that would be new for a slave; חליפין is not new because it works for movables.

steps.title: שמואל: a slave can be acquired through משיכה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that a עבד כנעני is acquired through משיכה, and explains how it works.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: a עבד כנעני is acquired through pulling. How? If he grabbed him and the slave came to him, he acquired him. If he called him and the slave came to him, he did not acquire him.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל adds that pulling, the usual way to acquire movable objects, also works for a slave. He then explains what counts as pulling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grabbing the slave and bringing him over counts as pulling. But if the slave comes on his own after being called, that does not count, because the buyer did not move him.

keyTerms.meaning: Pulling; acquiring something by moving it toward yourself

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
A Canaanite slave is acquired through pulling.
How? If he took hold of him and he came to him, he acquired him.
If he called him and he came to him, he did not acquire him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: עֶבֶד כְּנַעֲנִי נִקְנֶה בִּמְשִׁיכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds yet another method, after the ברייתא added חליפין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A עבד כנעני is acquired through משיכה, but only when grabbed, not when he comes after being called.

steps.title: Why doesn't the ברייתא list משיכה?
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה's silence about משיכה is understandable, but the ברייתא that lists חליפין should list משיכה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for our תנא: he doesn't teach methods that work for movables, only methods that don't. But the outside תנא should teach pulling!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts why our משנה leaves out משיכה, but challenges the ברייתא for leaving it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה's rule from step 18 explains skipping משיכה, which works for movables. But the ברייתא already lists חליפין, a method that works for movables. So why didn't it also list משיכה?

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense for (this side), but...
The outside תנא, the author of the ברייתא

phrases.english: It makes sense according to our tanna:
a matter that applies to movable property, he does not teach;
one that does not apply to movable property, he teaches.
But according to the outside tanna, let him teach pulling!
phrases.notes: The 'outside tanna' is the author of the ברייתא from step 16, who added חליפין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses שמואל's ruling to challenge the ברייתא's list.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא that adds only חליפין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא already lists a method that works for movables, so it should also list משיכה.

steps.title: The ברייתא only lists methods that work for both land and movables
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists methods that work for both land and movables; משיכה works only for movables, so it is left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he teaches, he teaches methods that work for both land and movables. Pulling, which works for movables but not for land, he does not teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא has its own rule for what to list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חליפין works for both land and movables, so the ברייתא lists it. משיכה works only for movables and not for land, so the ברייתא skips it. Each תנא has a different reason for choosing his list.

phrases.english: When he teaches, a matter that applies
both to land and to movable property;
pulling, which applies to movable property
but does not apply to land, he does not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָתָנֵי, מִילְּתָא דְּאִיתַהּ בֵּין בִּמְקַרְקְעֵי בֵּין בְּמִטַּלְטְלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines what the ברייתא chose to include
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא should have listed משיכה alongside חליפין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא lists only methods that work for both land and movables, and משיכה does not work for land.
steps.whatToRemember: Each source picks its list by a different rule: the משנה lists methods that do not work for movables, and the ברייתא lists methods that work for both land and movables.

steps.title: Quoting שמואל's rule again to examine it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats שמואל's explanation of grabbing versus calling, to look at it more closely.
steps.simpleTranslation: How? If he grabbed him and he came to him, he acquired him. If he called him and he came to him, he did not acquire him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to שמואל's words from step 19. It is setting up a challenge to the second half, about calling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is said here. The גמרא repeats the rule because the next step will question whether calling really does not acquire.

keyTerms.meaning: How? (in what way does this work)

phrases.english: How? If he took hold of him and he came to him, he acquired him;
if he called him and he came to him, he did not acquire him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the discussion of the lists to שמואל's own words.

steps.title: Does calling really not work? A ברייתא about animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule that calling does not acquire, and starts quoting a ברייתא about acquiring an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: And calling doesn't work? But it was taught: how is an animal acquired through handing over? If he grabbed it by its hoof, its hair, the saddle on it, the load on it, the bit in its mouth, or the bell on its neck, he acquired it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions שמואל's rule about calling and brings a ברייתא on how animals are acquired. The ברייתא is not finished here; the challenge continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the ברייתא lists the ways to grab an animal for מסירה. The quote goes on to explain משיכה of an animal, which is where the actual difficulty with שמואל will show up.

keyTerms.meaning: Handing over; acquiring an animal by grabbing part of it

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the challenge is already finished here. The ברייתא lines quoted so far are about grabbing an animal; the part that actually clashes with שמואל comes in the next lines.

phrases.english: And calling him does not acquire?
But it was taught: How is it done through handing over?
If he grabbed it by its hoof, by its hair,
by the saddle on it, by the load on it,
by the bit in its mouth, or by the bell on its neck, he acquired it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second half of שמואל's rule, just repeated.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that calling a slave does not acquire him
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא on acquiring animals is brought to show that calling may work; the key line comes as the quote continues.

steps.title: The ברייתא: calling an animal counts as pulling
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says an animal is acquired through משיכה even when the owner only calls it and it comes. This challenges שמואל's rule that calling does not acquire.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does pulling work? He calls the animal and it comes, or he hits it with a stick and it runs in front of him. Once it lifts a front leg and a back leg, he owns it. רבי אסי (some say רבי אחא) says it must walk in front of him the length of its own body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא it began in the last step. The ברייתא shows that calling an animal works as משיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said calling a slave does not acquire him. This ברייתא says calling an animal does acquire it. So the challenge is: why should calling work for an animal but not for a slave?

keyTerms.meaning: He hit it with a stick
It lifted a front leg and a back leg
The full length of its body

phrases.english: How is it acquired by pulling?
He calls it and it comes,
or he hit it with a stick and it ran in front of him,
once it lifted a front leg and a back leg, he acquired it.
phrases.notes: For an animal, "hand" means a front leg.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אַסִּי וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי אַחָא אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi, and some say Rabbi Acha, says:
Not until it walks in front of him the full length of its body.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד בִּמְשִׁיכָה? קוֹרֵא לָהּ וְהִיא בָּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא that step 23 began quoting as a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that calling a slave does not acquire him
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says calling an animal counts as משיכה, so calling a slave should count too.

steps.title: An animal follows its master; a slave follows himself
steps.stepSummary: Calling works for an animal because it walks by its owner's will. A slave walks by his own will, so his coming does not count as the master's act.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: an animal walks because its master wants it to. A slave walks because he himself wants to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that a slave and an animal are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When an animal comes at its owner's call, the owner is really the one moving it, so it counts as pulling. A slave decides on his own to come, so the master has done no act of acquiring.

keyTerms.meaning: By the will of its master

phrases.english: They say: an animal walks by the will of its master,
but a slave walks by his own will.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא about the animal.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between the cases (animal vs. slave)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Calling should work for a slave just as it works for an animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: Calling works only when the one who comes is moving by the owner's will, so it does not work for an adult slave.

steps.title: A minor slave is like an animal
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says a slave who is a minor is treated like an animal, so calling him does acquire him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: a young slave is like an animal.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds a limit to the answer just given. A child slave does not have his own will in this sense, so he is like an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer was based on the slave walking by his own will. A minor does not have a mind of his own in this way. So for him, calling works just like it does for an animal.

keyTerms.meaning: A slave who is a minor

steps.whatToRemember: Calling counts as משיכה for an animal and a minor slave, because they move by the master's will. It does not count for an adult slave, who moves by his own will.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
A slave who is a minor is like an animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: עֶבֶד קָטָן כִּבְהֵמָה דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the answer's logic to a minor slave.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A minor slave can be acquired by calling, just like an animal.

steps.title: How a slave is acquired through חזקה
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא lists acts of service that acquire a slave for the master: removing his shoe, carrying his things to the bathhouse, washing, dressing, lifting him, and more.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: How is a slave acquired through חזקה? If the slave took off the master's shoe, or carried his things after him to the bathhouse, undressed him, washed him, rubbed him with oil, scraped him, dressed him, put on his shoes, or lifted him, the master acquires him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא that explains the method of חזקה for a slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a slave, חזקה means the slave does a personal service for the new master. Each act on the list shows the slave is now serving him. Lifting the master is also on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: Acquiring through an act of possession; for a slave, serving the master

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: How is it acquired through possession?
If he untied his shoe for him,
phrases.notes: The slave is doing these things for the master who is buying him.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ הוֹלִיךְ כֵּלָיו אַחֲרָיו לְבֵית הַמֶּרְחָץ,
phrases.english: or carried his things after him to the bathhouse,
undressed him, washed him, rubbed him with oil, scraped him,
dressed him, put on his shoes, lifted him, the master acquires him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from משיכה to a new method, חזקה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave is acquired when he does a personal service for the master, including lifting him.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: חזקה is not stronger than lifting
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says חזקה should not be stronger than הגבהה, since lifting acquires in every situation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: חזקה should not be greater than lifting, because lifting acquires everywhere.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי שמעון's view about lifting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון points out that lifting is a method that works for every kind of property. So it should work for a slave too. At this point it is not yet clear how he differs from the first opinion.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said:
Possession should not be greater than lifting,
for lifting acquires in every situation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: לֹא תְּהֵא חֲזָקָה גְּדוֹלָה מֵהַגְבָּהָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second opinion inside the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lifting acquires a slave, since lifting acquires everything.

steps.title: What is רבי שמעון adding?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי שמעון means, since the first opinion already listed lifting.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי שמעון is adding. This sets up the next step, where רב אשי explains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא already said "הגביהו – קנאו." So it looks like רבי שמעון is saying the same thing. The גמרא wants to know where they disagree.

phrases.english: What is he saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how רבי שמעון's statement differs from the first opinion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי שמעון disagrees with the תנא קמא, who also mentioned lifting.

steps.title: רב אשי: who lifts whom
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the תנא קמא means the slave lifting the master acquires him, but the master lifting the slave does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: If the slave lifted his master, the master acquires him. If the master lifted the slave, he does not acquire him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question by reading the תנא קמא's "lifted him" as the slave lifting the master.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, lifting works only as a service, so the slave must be the one doing it. If the master lifts the slave, the slave has served no one. So for the תנא קמא that does not acquire.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
If he lifted his master, the master acquires him,
if his master lifted him, the master does not acquire him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הִגְבִּיהוֹ הוּא לְרַבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא קמא accepts only the slave lifting the master, as a service; the master lifting the slave does not work.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: even the master lifting the slave acquires
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats רבי שמעון's words, now understood as disagreeing: the master lifting the slave also acquires him, since lifting acquires everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: חזקה should not be greater than lifting, because lifting acquires everywhere.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רבי שמעון's words to show what they mean now. He is arguing that even if the master lifts the slave, he acquires him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words are the same as in step 28, but now we know the point. The תנא קמא sees lifting only as a service, but רבי שמעון sees it as a normal method of acquiring. So the master lifting the slave works, just as lifting works for any object.
steps.whatToRemember: תנא קמא: only the slave lifting the master acquires (as service). רבי שמעון: the master lifting the slave also acquires, because lifting acquires everything.
steps.confusionAlert: This is the same sentence as step 28, not a new statement. The גמרא repeats it so we can read it with רב אשי's explanation in mind.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said:
Possession should not be greater than lifting,
phrases.notes: He means: if service acts already acquire the slave, then the master lifting him, which acquires anything, should surely work too.

phrases.english: for lifting acquires in every situation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: לֹא תְּהֵא חֲזָקָה גְּדוֹלָה מֵהַגְבָּהָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב אשי's explanation by rereading רבי שמעון's words against the תנא קמא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי שמעון holds that a master acquires a slave even by lifting him himself, because lifting is a method that acquires everything.

steps.title: Should a maidservant then be acquired through intercourse?
steps.stepSummary: If a slave lifting his master makes the master acquire him, then a שפחה כנענית should be acquired through ביאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you said that if the slave lifts his master, the master acquires him, then a Canaanite maidservant should be acquired through intercourse!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule from Step 30, that a slave lifting his master makes the master acquire him. If that is true, ביאה should also work as a קנין for a שפחה כנענית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule says the slave doing something for the master, such as lifting him, creates the קנין. During ביאה the maidservant is also, in a sense, holding up the master. So the rule seems to lead to a strange result that nobody accepts.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you said. This takes an earlier rule and pushes it further.
If so, then... This introduces a result that seems impossible.

phrases.english: Now that you have said:
if he lifts his master, the master acquires him,
phrases.notes: This is רב אשי's reading from Step 30: the slave does the lifting.

phrases.english: if so, from now on
a Canaanite maidservant should be acquired through intercourse?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמְרַתְּ הִגְבִּיהוֹ הוּא לְרַבּוֹ קְנָאוֹ אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the lifting rule from Steps 30-31 and tests where it leads.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a slave lifting his master is a קנין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Applying the same idea to ביאה gives a result that is not accepted, so the rule must be limited somehow.

steps.title: A service act works only when the master benefits and the slave makes an effort
steps.stepSummary: A service-קנין needs the master to benefit and the slave to make an effort. In ביאה both sides benefit, so it is not a קנין.
steps.simpleTranslation: When we say this, it is where this one benefits and that one suffers. Here, this one benefits and that one benefits too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by explaining what makes a service act acquire a slave. In ביאה that key feature is missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A service act shows ownership when the master enjoys the act and the slave works hard for him. In ביאה both people benefit, so the act does not show the master's authority over her. This is why it cannot serve as a קנין.

keyTerms.meaning: When we said [the rule]. This narrows when a rule applies.
This one benefits and that one suffers

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the basic reason a service act creates a קנין for a slave: the master benefits from the slave's effort.

phrases.english: When we say [that service acquires],
it is where this one benefits and that one suffers,
phrases.notes: The master gets the benefit, while the slave does the hard work.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא: זֶה נֶהֱנֶה וְזֶה נֶהֱנֶה הוּא.
phrases.english: here it is a case where this one benefits and that one benefits.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָאָמְרִינַן זֶה נֶהֱנֶה וְזֶה מִצְטַעֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the rule by adding a condition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any physical act the slave does for the master is a קנין, including ביאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only an act where the master benefits and the slave makes an effort is a קנין. ביאה benefits both, so it does not count.

steps.title: What about intercourse in an unusual manner?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about ביאה שלא כדרכה, where it seems only the man benefits.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is in an unusual manner, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer in Step 33. It points to a kind of ביאה where the woman seems not to benefit at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 33 depended on both sides benefiting. In a case שלא כדרכה only the man seems to benefit, so it looks like a case of 'this one benefits and that one suffers.' Then it should be a קנין after all.

keyTerms.meaning: Not in the usual manner (atypical intercourse)
What is there to say? A follow-up challenge to an answer.

phrases.english: [If it is] in an unusual manner,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 33.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that in ביאה both sides benefit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In ביאה שלא כדרכה only the man seems to benefit, so the condition for a קנין seems to be met.

steps.title: Who says both do not benefit?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחיי בר אדא answers that we cannot assume only one side benefits, even שלא כדרכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחיי בר אדא of אחא said: Who will tell us that there is no benefit for both of them?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחיי gives his first answer. He rejects the assumption behind the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that in a case שלא כדרכה the woman does not benefit. רב אחיי says that is not proven. If both may benefit, the reasoning of Step 33 still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Who will tell us? It is not clear at all.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחַיי [בַּר אַדָּא] דְּמִן אַחָא:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥai [bar Adda] of Aḥa said:
phrases.notes: Some versions add the words in square brackets. אחא is the name of his town.

phrases.english: Who will tell us
that there is not benefit for both of them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 34.

steps.title: The פסוק treats both kinds of intercourse the same
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the plural 'משכבי אשה' links ביאה כדרכה with שלא כדרכה, so they follow the same law.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, 'lyings of a woman' is written. The פסוק compares the usual manner to the unusual manner.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחיי adds a second answer, this time from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the plural word 'משכבי', which shows there are two kinds of ביאה with a woman. Since the תורה puts them together, ביאה שלא כדרכה gets the same law as the usual kind. Usual ביאה is not a קנין, so the unusual kind is not one either.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore. This introduces a second answer.
'Lyings of a woman.' The plural form shows two kinds of intercourse.
The פסוק compared it. One case gets the law of the other.

steps.whatToRemember: ביאה never acquires a שפחה כנענית. A service-קנין needs the master to benefit and the slave to make an effort, and the תורה treats both kinds of ביאה alike.

phrases.english: And furthermore: "lyings of a woman" is written,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:22. The word is plural, which points to two ways.

phrases.english: the verse compared the usual manner to the unusual manner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second answer to the challenge of Step 34.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Linking the two cases through a פסוק (היקש)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ביאה שלא כדרכה might be treated differently from usual ביאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק joins the two kinds, so neither one is a קנין.

steps.title: מר זוטרא acquires the slave of a dying convert
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה הנדואה, a גר with no heirs, was dying. מר זוטרא told his slave to take off his shoes and bring them to his house, which is an act of service.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה from India was a convert with no heirs. He became ill, and מר זוטרא came to visit him. He saw he was very close to death, and said to his slave: Take off my shoes and bring them to my house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows the service-קנין from Step 27 being used in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a גר with no heirs dies, his property becomes ownerless, and the first person to take it acquires it. Removing the master's shoes and carrying his things are the service acts listed in Step 27. מר זוטרא used them so the slave would become his once רבי יהודה died.

keyTerms.meaning: A convert with no heirs. His property becomes ownerless when he dies.
To ask after him, to visit a sick person
The world was pressing on him. He was near death.
Take off my shoes for me

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda from India
was a convert who had no heirs.

phrases.aramaic: חֲלַשׁ, עָל מָר זוּטְרָא לְשַׁיּוֹלֵי בֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: He became ill; Mar Zutra went in to ask about his health,
he saw that the world was pressing on him very much.
phrases.notes: This means he was about to die.

phrases.english: He said to his slave:
phrases.notes: He spoke to רבי יהודה's slave, not his own.

and bring them to the house.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִנְדּוּאָה גֵּר שֶׁאֵין לוֹ יוֹרְשִׁין הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ביאה discussion and tells a story that applies the service-קנין of Step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A service act, like removing shoes and carrying them home, is used to acquire a slave from an ownerless estate.

steps.title: Some say the slave was an adult
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to report a disagreement about the story: some say the slave was an adult.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are those who say he was an adult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It starts reporting views about whether the slave in the story was an adult or a child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The slave's age matters for how he could be acquired. That explanation continues in the text that comes next. Here the גמרא only gives the first view: the slave was a גדול.

phrases.english: There are those who say
he was an adult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a detail about the story in Step 37 and sets up a discussion of the slave's age.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to one view, the slave in the story was an adult.
